questions.text: What is the asymptotic solution of T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n log n, with T(1) = 1?
questions.explain: This is the Master Theorem borderline case extended: with a = 2, b = 2, n^(log_b a) = n, and the driving function is n log n = n log^1 n. The result is n log^(1+1) n = n log^2 n.

questions.text: What is the asymptotic solution of T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n^2?
questions.explain: a = 4, b = 2, so n^(log_2 4) = n^2, which matches the driving function exactly. Case 2 of the Master Theorem gives Theta(n^2 log n).

questions.text: What is the minimum number of comparisons needed in the worst case to find both the minimum and the maximum of 100 distinct elements?
questions.explain: Pair up the elements and compare within pairs (n/2 comparisons), then find the min among the smaller halves and the max among the larger halves (n/2 - 1 each). Total = 3n/2 - 2 = 150 - 2 = 148.

questions.text: Which sorting algorithms have worst-case time complexity O(n log n)? Select all that apply.
options: Quick sort with a fixed last-element pivot
questions.explain: Merge sort and heap sort are O(n log n) in the worst case. Quick sort with a fixed pivot degrades to O(n^2) on sorted input, and insertion sort is O(n^2).

questions.text: Why can Dijkstra's algorithm fail on a graph containing negative edge weights, even when there is no negative cycle?
options: The priority queue cannot store negative keys
A vertex may be finalised before a cheaper path through a later-relaxed vertex is discovered
It fails only when the graph is disconnected
questions.explain: Dijkstra's correctness relies on the greedy invariant that the minimum tentative distance is final. A negative edge can reduce a path after its endpoint has been finalised, breaking that invariant. Bellman-Ford handles this case.

questions.text: Which statements about minimum spanning trees of a connected weighted graph are true? Select all that apply.
options: If all edge weights are distinct, the MST is unique
The lightest edge of the graph belongs to some MST
The MST always contains the shortest path between every pair of vertices
Every MST has exactly V - 1 edges
questions.explain: Distinct weights force a unique MST, the globally lightest edge is always safe by the cut property, and any spanning tree of V vertices has V - 1 edges. MSTs minimise total weight, not pairwise distances.

questions.text: Two sequences have lengths m and n. What are the time and space complexities of the standard dynamic programming solution for the longest common subsequence, using full table construction?
options: O(m + n) time, O(m + n) space
O(m log n) time, O(n) space
questions.explain: The table has (m+1)(n+1) cells, each filled in constant time, so O(mn) for both. Space drops to O(min(m, n)) if only the LCS length is needed, since each row depends on the previous row alone.

questions.text: For which problem does a greedy strategy fail to give an optimal solution in general?
options: Fractional knapsack, taking items by decreasing value per unit weight
0/1 knapsack, taking items by decreasing value per unit weight
Huffman coding, merging the two lowest-frequency nodes
Activity selection, choosing the earliest finishing activity
questions.explain: The 0/1 knapsack has no greedy optimal solution because items cannot be split, so a high-density item may block a better combination. It needs dynamic programming. The other three are classic correct greedy algorithms.

questions.text: In a depth-first search of a directed graph, the presence of which edge type proves the graph has a cycle?
questions.explain: A back edge points to an ancestor still on the recursion stack, which closes a cycle. Forward and cross edges can appear in acyclic directed graphs.

questions.text: Problem A is NP-complete and reduces in polynomial time to problem B. What can be concluded about B?
questions.explain: The reduction makes B at least as hard as A, so B is NP-hard. Calling B NP-complete additionally requires B to be in NP, which was not stated.
